Lozova Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Lozova emerged around a railway station in the late 1860s; by 1897, its Jewish population reached 813 (22 percent), though Jews were not officially permitted to settle there until 1903. The town's synagogue, first mentioned in 1913, was closed by Soviet authorities and converted into a church in December 1941 under German occupation, later becoming a youth center, then a library, before its demolition in the late 1970s. This cemetery's establishment date is unknown and it does not appear on old regional maps; per local residents, its remnants were finally destroyed around 2010 during construction of an enterprise on the site.
